World.title: Careless waste handling attracts rodents to the city
World.content:
The Põhja‑Tallinn district government is collecting tips about rat and mouse activity through mid‑August to direct pest control efforts to the most affected areas. Experts say careless waste handling encourages rodent spread.

Kadri Karnau, communications specialist at the Tallinn Environment and Public Works Department, said the city does not gather centralized statistics on rodent numbers because they cannot be reliably assessed. Still, residents' observations are welcome because they help identify larger colonies.

Rodent control in the capital is divided by areas of responsibility, meaning homeowners' associations play an important role. "When a colony is discovered, the first step is to speak with the private property owner or the homeowners' association, which is responsible for rodent control. The city and district government can only carry out control on areas they manage," Karnau said.

The Environment and Public Works Department uses rat poison placed in special plastic boxes. Karnau said districts do not conduct large‑scale preventive poisoning because it would pose a danger to pets, birds and people. Control is always targeted and based on specific nesting sites and movement paths.

Ettevõtmise eesmärk on leida üles kõige probleemsemad ja pahategelikud rotid. Autor/allikas: slyfox photography/Unsplash

Joosep Sarapuu, a zoologist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, said local control will not eliminate rodents from the city. "It is not possible in practice to achieve 100‑percent eradication of rats. When one colony disappears, the area becomes freely accessible to newcomers again," he said.

Rat control is complicated by their biological behavior. They exhibit neophobia, meaning fear of new objects. When a plastic box with poison or a trap appears, rodents need time before they dare to approach it.

A common belief that colonies send their weakest members to test poison is not entirely accurate, Sarapuu said. "Dominant individuals do not check new things because they have established routes and a stable food supply. Lower‑ranking members are forced to look for new feeding sites and movement paths. That is why they are the first to encounter poison and traps," he said.

Joosep Sarapuu. Source: ERR

How can people keep rodents away from their homes? Sarapuu said summer is a good time to check a home's rodent‑proofing because pests try to enter houses when the weather gets cold. "You should find small gaps and openings where rats and mice can get inside and seal them carefully. Second, you must check food waste to make sure it is not easily accessible. In that case, rodents are likely to be fewer or not present at all," he said.

Karnau also said a tidy neighborhood is the best way to keep rodents away. "Trash rooms and waste containers must be kept in good condition and closed to prevent food waste from spreading into the surroundings. It is also wise to avoid feeding birds and squirrels and to keep the areas under bird feeders clean because fallen food attracts rodents," she said.

World.title: Expert: Talk of a direct Russian attack is extremely foolish
World.content:
Claims by anonymous American intelligence sources that a possible limited Russian attack against NATO may happen in the coming years are exaggerated speculation, said security expert Rainer Saks, former secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2015-2020) and the Foreign Intellegence Service (2011-2015).

ERR: A U.S. intelligence assessment has been published by The Wall Street Journal, stating that Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whose invasion of Ukraine has stalled, could test NATO in the coming years by attacking one of the alliance's member states. The report mentions both cyberattacks and a limited ground incursion. What should we make of all this?

Rainer Saks: First of all, this is another classic case where anonymous sources have said something, fragments have been written down, but official comments are either unavailable or refused. It is a very broad and diffuse text.

As for these general assessments that Russia "could do something," there is no significant indication behind them that Russia is actually planning to do so. It is a hypothetical assessment that Russia could do this, that or the other. As long as Russia is not planning such actions, publishing assessments like this in the current context actually works very much in Russia's favor. Even the suggested time frame, from this autumn until 2029, is completely absurd.

Russia is certainly not making plans like that.

It is difficult to judge whether this was leaked by the U.S. government or is the initiative of an individual intelligence official. We will not speculate about that, but this is speculation rather than a report based on a concrete intelligence assessment.

The proposed actions — from cyberattacks to a limited military incursion — essentially cover the entire range of scenarios that could theoretically be considered. Therefore, I would not take this at present as a serious warning requiring the rapid implementation of countermeasures.

For example, Russia has been carrying out cyberattacks against NATO member states continuously since at least 2005–2006.

At the same time, NATO countries' responses have so far not been appropriate, because before the invasion of Ukraine, several European countries sought to engage Russia and develop energy cooperation instead. Examples of the kind of situation described in the intelligence report can also be found 15 to 20 years ago, so there is nothing new in it.

At the moment, publishing such a report works more to Russia's advantage, because Russia itself has not directly threatened NATO countries with any military action. Instead, a context is now being created that allows it to manipulate information even more than it has done so far.

In that sense, I think the text published by The Wall Street Journal is extremely foolish.

The article also points to indications that Russia is already testing NATO's response, for example, drones and missiles have fallen on the territory of Romania and Poland. This is presented as one indication that perhaps something is underway.

At the same time, those very countries have themselves said that they do not regard this as deliberate Russian action, but rather as accidental or technical incidents. I cannot say whether the official comments differ drastically from what is actually happening.

This is, of course, a problem because while active warfare is taking place in Ukraine, the possibility of, for example, Ukrainian drones ending up in allied territory or being shot down there is indeed an elevated risk.

There are only two main scenarios under which Russia would begin testing NATO's unity.

The first is that NATO has completely fallen apart internally. Although NATO's unity has suffered in several respects recently, there is no full political unity and there are sharp disagreements between different member states, it cannot be said that there is no unity at all. I would not yet go so far as to claim that NATO's collective defense has therefore been called into question.

The domestic political problems of member states and NATO's internal weakening are, in fact, the most likely scenario that could lead to a military confrontation between Russia and a NATO member state. At the moment, however, that process is clearly not advancing rapidly.

The second theoretical possibility is that if Russia truly decides to attack NATO militarily, it would first have to reorganize its forces. For such an attack — or even a test — to be genuinely supported, Russia would most likely have to carry out a mobilization. To some extent, that is theoretically possible after the State Duma elections, because the forces fighting against Ukraine have been unable to achieve success, and according to the Russian General Staff's calculations, there are too few troops.

In a situation where a full-scale war is still being fought in Ukraine, launching a new war against an even stronger opponent would, in my view, require Russia to declare martial law and carry out full-scale mobilization. That is something without which I do not believe Russia would proceed with very aggressive plans.

The article repeatedly refers to the fact that the Americans are running low on missile stockpiles because of operations in the Middle East and donations to Ukraine. Could it instead be that this article and the intelligence assessment are aimed at a domestic U.S. audience, to remind people of the need to replenish weapons stockpiles quickly?

That may indeed be the case. However, there is one important nuance here: the issue is not that the United States lacks certain types of missiles in its stockpiles, primarily air defense missiles and Tomahawk-type long-range strike weapons, of which too many have been expended against Iran. It is natural for stockpiles to decline during active military operations, but production is reportedly not keeping pace with what is needed. That is an embarrassing situation — what is the point of launching military operations if you cannot simultaneously replenish your stocks?

What is being overlooked, however, is that Russia has exactly the same problem, only even more severe. It also lacks sufficient air defense capabilities, as demonstrated by the success of Ukraine's long-range strikes. For example, this morning yet another large Wildberries warehouse, deep in the Urals some 1,800 kilometers from Ukraine, was set on fire.

Russia is in exactly the same position of weakness. Its entire missile capability is focused on Ukraine, and it is unable to carry out large-scale missile strikes on a daily basis. The war has lasted four years and has significantly exhausted Russia.

Of course, we can talk about hybrid attacks, but the conditions for Russia to launch a military incursion into NATO territory or start a military conflict with NATO are in no way favorable for Russia at present.

Why do you think intelligence assessments claiming that Russia is about to start testing NATO keep being published, when in reality they do not correspond to the facts?

I cannot answer that question. It is probably influenced by many different factors, ranging from incompetence and foolishness to domestic political objectives.

There is, of course, genuine reason to be concerned about the overall situation. There is nothing good about it. A major war is underway, and the governments of Europe and the United States have been unable to bring it to an end. That is indeed a very serious problem. Supporting Ukraine has also not been as successful as it should have been — a great deal has been done, but not enough.

A separate question is why European leaders have been unable to pull themselves together. Four years after the start of the full-scale war, they are still unable to produce enough of the military equipment that is needed. That is a very bad sign. In that sense, it is understandable that many people are seriously concerned about the situation and are trying to warn of possible negative developments.

World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
World.content:
Akal Takht panel flags Punjab govt response, seeks compliance report on anti-sacrilege law

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The expert panel appointed by the Akal Takht on Friday asked the Punjab government to first submit a compliance report on the objections raised by the Sikh temporal seat before any further talks on the proposed anti-sacrilege law.The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht, especially those related to possible interference in Sikh religious matters.On June 29, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj had given the state government one month to respond to his objections to the anti-sacrilege law.In a statement on Friday, the Akal Takht secretariat said the government's response, submitted just before the deadline, was an attempt to avoid the main issues. It said the concerns of the Sikh community had already been conveyed to the Punjab assembly Speaker and members of the state Cabinet on July 31.The secretariat also accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of not taking a constructive approach towards resolving the sensitive issue.It said that despite being given enough time, the Punjab government had not formed its own panel to discuss the matter.Earlier, Jathedar Gargajj had rejected the government's response as "unsatisfactory" and announced a five-member expert panel to hold discussions with the Aam Aadmi Party government.The panel includes retired judges Rupinder Singh Sodhi and Mohinder Mohan Singh Bedi, senior advocate Puran Singh Hundal, and Sikh scholars Dr Kehar Singh and Prof Jagmohan Singh.The Jathedar had also written to Punjab assembly Speaker Kultar Singh, Sikh MLAs and state ministers, asking them not to discuss or amend the anti-sacrilege law without a wider "Panthic" consensus.He had directed Sikh MLAs and Cabinet ministers to ensure that no discussion on the law takes place during the assembly session that began on August 3 until an agreement is reached with the Akal Takht and the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC).The issue came up after AAP MLA Inderbir Singh Nijjar submitted the Punjab government's response to the objections raised by the Akal Takht over the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation.

World.title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025, even as blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting continued challenges in blood inventory management despite a steady rise in donations.

Available official data indicate that China and India are among the world's largest blood collection programmes. In 2025, India collected 15.71 million units of blood, while China collected 25.5 million units, according to China's National Health Commission.

The data, reported by blood centres through the government's e-Raktakosh portal, show that expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units and other operational reasons.

Reason-wise discard data has been captured on the portal since 2024, while such details were not available for 2023.

Replying to a question in Parliament, the Union health ministry, however, said it had not received any report of regional blood shortages. It added that ensuring an adequate supply of safe blood and minimising wastage is primarily the responsibility of state governments and Union Territories, while the Centre advocates a hub-and-spoke model under which blood is collected and processed at high-volume centres before being distributed to smaller blood banks and storage centres.





According to the data, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest blood collection in 2025 with 21.6 lakh units, followed by Maharashtra (18.73 lakh), Gujarat (11.82 lakh), Rajasthan (10.79 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (9.74 lakh). Overall blood collection increased from 1.42 crore units in 2023 to 1.58 crore units in 2025.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The annexure also showed a corresponding increase in blood component utilisation, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan reporting the highest utilisation during 2025.

At the same time, Uttar Pradesh reported the highest discard of blood components at 2.40 lakh, followed by Maharashtra (1.87 lakh), Kerala (1.44 lakh), Rajasthan (1.21 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (1.09 lakh). The ministry did not provide an analysis of the wide variation in discard across states.

Dr Hema Goyal, Consultant (Blood centre & Lab services), Aakash healthcare said blood wastage is inevitable to some extent, particularly because platelets have a shelf life of only five days. But discarding 17.4 lakh blood components in a year points to a mismatch between collection and actual demand. The solution is not fewer donations but smarter inventory management through real-time stock sharing and better coordination between blood banks.

World.title: FSSAI pulls up two popular food products over safety, compliance lapses
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a fresh crackdown on food safety violations, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products, penalising the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard and stopping the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.

The regulator imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd, Mangaluru, after a laboratory analysis of a retail sample of Fortune "Fryola" Refined Sunflower Seed Oil found that its vitamin D content was below the prescribed standard, making the fortified edible oil substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

FSSAI said the company was given an opportunity to present its case, but the adjudicating authority concluded that it had manufactured and marketed a substandard fortified edible oil before imposing a monetary penalty.

In a separate action, the regulator prohibited the sale of PIE Foods' Monk Fruit Sweetener, a natural zero-calorie sugar substitute, after inspections found cartons of the product stored at the company's premises without the required manufacturing licence.

FSSAI also alleged that the product carried claims such as "100% Monk Fruit Extract" and "Natural Ingredients", while its online listing did not carry the mandatory endorsement required under food safety regulations.





It further said the company failed to produce records showing that the monk fruit extract used in the product had been procured in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.

The prohibition order will remain in force until the product complies with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.

The regulator said the actions are part of its ongoing drive to tighten enforcement against food business operators and ensure that products sold to consumers meet prescribed safety and quality standards.

World.title: India digest: Nagpur flat owner booked in minor rape case; CBI charges 11 in Suvendu PA case
World.content:
Nagpur minor rape: Flat owner to face FIR

The owner of a one-room flat, where a 16-year-old Class 12 student was held captive for 24 hours and subjected to brutal sexual assault by a Thane youth, is set to face an FIR for not verifying his tenant, who posed as a NEET aspirant while seeking the rented room, said police.

The acÂ­cused booked the room for Rs 3,000 through an online portal and was in possession of it for three months.

World.title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With former Bangladesh PM

âs news conference kicking up a diplomatic firestorm, the government said on Friday her remarks, especially those related to the government in Dhaka, are not endorsed by India.

World.title: Ex-HC judge on West Bengal SIR tribunal in Supreme Court seeking protection
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A former Calcutta high court judge who is presiding over one of the SIR appellate tribunals on Friday sought protection from the Supreme Court, claiming that before elections, she and her family members were repeatedly given life threats and their home CCTV connections were disconnected by miscreants.

The petitioner, who is the advocate son of former judge Anindita Roy Saraswati, complained that the first threat letter was delivered at her residence on May 30, another on May 2, followed by cutting of the wires of CCTV cameras at their Kolkata residence.

The petitioner said despite complaints to the Bidhannagar police commissionerate seeking a threat assessment, police protection, and forensic examination of the threat letters, no effective protection was provided to the former judge or her family members.

The petition sought transfer of the investigations to the SC-monitored SIT.

World.title: BJP picks audio clip to target Congress over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday seized on a leaked conversation allegedly between two Congress functionaries to claim that money was exchanged for ministerial berths in the recent expansion of the Karnataka cabinet and demanded replies from Congressâ Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.

BJP MP Anurag Thakurâs attack on Congress came after Karnataka BJPâs Chalavadi Narayanaswamy cited the audio record to allege that cabinet positions in the state had been secured through monetary influence. According to the audio tape of the conversation, 80% of the ministers secured their posts in the state cabinet by making such offerings, he added.

âIn Congress, oneâs stature and chair depend on the offering they make to its high command,â he said and cited the audio to wonder if a senior Congress functionary like HK Patil was denied a berth because he did not pay the bribe.

âThe question is why a person, who is an accused in the Valmiki Tribes Development Corporation scam and is still facing an ED case, has been inducted into the cabinet?â Thakur asked, in an apparent reference to B Nagendra.

World.title: 16,357 govt. schools functioning with single teacher in A.P., alleges Sharmila
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Y.S. Sharmila on Thursday said that 16,357 government schools in Andhra Pradesh are functioning with only one teacher each, describing it as the “true report card” of the NDA governments at the Centre and in the State.

In a post on X, Ms. Sharmila criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led Central government and the State government headed by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, alleging that while they had made tall promises about the future of education. But, they failed to address the shortage of teachers in government schools.

She said thousands of children were being deprived of the basic necessity of having a teacher in every classroom, despite repeated claims by the governments about improving the education sector.

Questioning the State government’s relationship with the Centre, Ms. Sharmila said Mr. Naidu often claimed to enjoy a special rapport with the Prime Minister. If that were the case, she asked, why Andhra Pradesh had failed to secure even the minimum support required to ensure adequate teacher strength in government schools.

The APCC chief contended that a government unable to provide a teacher for every school had no moral authority to speak about building the future of children.

She asserted that students needed teachers rather than publicity and maintained that Andhra Pradesh deserved justice instead of excuses from the governments.

World.title: Jharkhand student protest LIVE: Agitation enters 15th day, Govt. invites another faction for talks
World.content:
The students’ protest under the JPSS-JSCC Reform Manch over alleged irregularities in competitive exams entered its 15th day on Saturday (August 8, 2026) after talks between the State government and the student protestors failed to break the deadlock.

Also read: Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests

A delegation of the Jharkhand Government comprising Ministers on Friday (August 7, 2026) held talks for the first time in State capital Ranchi with student protestors demanding an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into alleged irregularities in competitive exams for government jobs. The two hour-long meeting, though, ended without any agreement with the students firm on continuing their protests. After the meeting with State govt on August 7, student leader Ravindra Paswan said: “It was the first round of meeting with the government and the government listened to our demands. However, we could not reach any conclusion regarding our key demands. Therefore, the protest will continue for the time being”.

Also read | Why are the students protesting in Ranchi? | Explained

The seven members delegation of another group headed by Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) will meet the committee formed by the government, on alleged irregularities in competitive exams, on Saturday (August 8).

World.title: Chennai Press Club seeks action against those involved in attack on journalists
World.content:
Journalists from several media organisations staged a protest at the Chennai Press Club on Thursday evening, condemning the recent attack on two journalists in Ranipet district, allegedly carried out at the behest of TVK’s Sholinghur MLA G. Kapil.

The protesters urged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to order an investigation and initiate criminal action against those responsible for the attack.

Speaking at the protest, N. Ram, veteran journalist and Director of The Hindu Group Publishing Private Limited, said: “Irrespective of whether a political party is in power or not, it is our duty to condemn such attacks. Our demand is that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay take this matter seriously, ascertain the truth, and ensure appropriate action. A proper investigation must be conducted, and suitable punishment should be awarded to those found guilty. An FIR is yet to be registered, and it should be done immediately.”

Nakkheeran Editor R.R. Gopal, Chennai Press Club president Suresh Vethanayagam, and general secretary Mohammed Aseef participated in the protest.

Mr. Vethanayagam said the journalists were only carrying out their professional duties and the assault was a direct attack on press freedom and the fundamental values of democracy.

Mr. Aseef alleged that the police remained passive instead of enforcing the law, and called for a comprehensive inquiry into the conduct of the police personnel present during the incident.

World.title: List of candidates selected for Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer posts released
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission (APPSC) on Thursday release the list of provisionally selected candidates for the post of Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer posts in the Sainik Welfare Service of the State.

The APPSC stated in a release that the provisional selection list pertaining to Notification No. 28/2025, dated September 24, 2025, and it has been made available on its official website for the information of candidates. Those who appeared for the recruitment process can check their provisional selection status on the Commission’s portal https://psc.ap.gov.in.

The Commission clarified that the provisional selection list has been published in accordance with the recruitment process notified earlier.

World.title: Greens urge Kerala government to adopt environmentally sustainable development model in ecologically fragile regions
World.content:
The Wayanad Prakruthi Samrakshana Samiti (WPSS) has urged the government and the public to adopt an environmentally sustainable development model in ecologically fragile regions such as Wayanad.

At a meeting held to commemorate the victims of the Mundakkai-Chooralmala landslide disaster on Thursday, the WPSS noted that the recurring landslides across the Western Ghats were nature’s response to unchecked and unscientific developments.

It said that large-scale quarrying, unscientific land use changes, tourism projects, and major infrastructure works had weakened the fragile ecosystem of Wayanad and contributed to repeated disasters. The WPSS reiterated its opposition to the Wayanad twin tunnel project, alleging that it was driven by commercial interests, including the extraction of valuable rock.

The Samiti said many survivors of the Mundakkai-Chooralmala disaster were still awaiting proper rehabilitation and adequate compensation for lost property and businesses, terming rehabilitation as a right rather than a government concession.

WPSS president N. Badusha presided.

World.title: Jharkhand protest: Stir enters 15th day, govt. invites another faction of agitators for talks
World.content:
The agitation over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, under the JPSS-JSCC Reform Manch entered its 15th day on Saturday (August 8, 2026) after talks between the State government and the student protesters failed to break the deadlock.

The seven-member delegation of another group headed by Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) will meet the committee formed by the government on Saturday (August 8, 2026). JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for seven days, is scheduled for talks with the government and had submitted the names of an eight-member delegation.

A delegation of the Jharkhand Government comprising Ministers on Friday (August 7, 2026) held talks for the first time in State capital Ranchi with student protestors demanding an inquiry by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into alleged irregularities in competitive exams. The two hour-long meeting, though, ended without any agreement with the students firm on continuing their protests.

After the meeting, student leader Ravindra Paswan said: “It was the first round of meeting with the government and the government listened to our demands. However, we could not reach any conclusion regarding our key demands. Therefore, the protest will continue for the time being.”

On the other hand, Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said, “The talks with the students took place in a positive atmosphere. All their points were heard and understood seriously, and the government will consider their demands before deciding on the next course of action.”

Earlier in the day, Chief Minister Hemant Soren told media persons that the government was ready for talks concerning the demands of the protesting students as hundreds have gathered at Ranchi’s Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium over the last two weeks.

The students are demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) exam and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities either by the CBI or by a panel of retired high court judges from outside the state, besides comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

The agitation, which began on July 25 under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, has grown into one of Jharkhand's largest student-led movements in recent years.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Haveri police return stolen property worth ₹2.30 crore to owners
World.content:
The Haveri police on Thursday returned stolen property worth about ₹2.30 crore to its rightful owners after solving 46 criminal cases, including various house break-ins and temple thefts in the district.

Addressing press persons in Haveri on Thursday, Superintendent of Police of Haveri district Yashodha Vantagodi said that the police had recovered gold ornaments worth ₹1.18 crore, cash amounting to ₹63.20 lakh, silver ornaments valued at ₹34.57 lakh, vehicles worth ₹8.68 lakh, mobile phones and other valuables between January and July.

She said that among the significant breakthroughs were the Makaravalli and Byadagi robbery cases, in which the accused was traced and arrested in Surat, Gujarat. In another burglary involving the theft of gold ornaments, the accused was traced to Madhya Pradesh.

“The Police Department is committed to ensuring justice for victims by tracing offenders and recovering stolen property,” Ms. Vantagodi said.

Responding to a question on the alleged cheating of maize trader Shivalingayya Gadigudal involving crores of rupees, Ms. Vantagodi said that the investigation into the case registered during 2021-22 had been completed and charge-sheet had been filed.

She further said that following the complainant’s request, the district police had submitted a proposal along with relevant records and was prepared to transfer the investigation to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

Additional Superintendent of Police Lakshman Shirakol and Deputy Superintendents of Police Girimall Talakatti, J. Lokesh and Gurushantappa K.V. were present.

Murder case solved

Ms. Vantagodi said that they have arrested a man in connection with the eight-month-old case of murder of a daily wage labourer in Koosagatti village in the Halageri Police Station limits in Ranebennur taluk.

Bodappa Ramappa Channagiri, 55, a resident of Masur village in Rattihalli taluk, was allegedly assaulted with stones and firewood and murdered at the Koosagatti bus stand on November 20, 2025. A special investigation team was constituted under the supervision of Additional Superintendent of Police Lakshman Shirakol and Deputy Superintendent of Police J. Lokesh.

The team, led by circle inspectorc Siddesh S.D. and Venkatesh and the Halageri Police Station sub-inspector Krishnakumar B. Mane, investigated the case using technical evidence and forensic inputs.

The investigation led to the arrest of Bharamappa Laxmappa Jogappanavar, 52, a resident of Adavi Anjaneya Layout in Ranebennur.

The police said forensic evidence corroborated his involvement in the crime. During questioning after his detention on July 28, the accused confessed to the offence, the Superintendent of Police said.

The accused had lent ₹20,000 to the deceased, who had repaid ₹10,000. A dispute over the remaining amount allegedly led to an altercation, culminating in the murder, she said.

The recovered property was displayed during the Property Return Parade before being handed over to the claimants for which requisite permissions from the court have been obtained.

First in South India

Meanwhile, Haveri district has topped South India for recovering maximum number of stolen mobiles phones. The Department of Telecommunication (DoT) of Government of India has released the ranking of districts in South India based on the number of mobile phones recovered through CEIR portal, and Haveri district has secured the first place.

Yashodha Vantagodi said that the DOT issued a letter of appreciation to the district during the Annual Security Conference for South Zone LSAs and LEAs held at Ernakulum in Kerala.

World.title: Amended resolution on Mekedatu Dam was put to vote and passed unanimously by the Legislative Assembly, Advocate General tells Madras High Court
World.content:
The amended resolution on Mekedatu Dam urging the Centre to constitute a special tribunal under Section 4 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 was put to vote in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and was passed unanimously by the House on June 19, 2026, Advocate General Vijay Narayan asserted before the Madras High Court on Thursday (July 30, 2026).

Appearing before the first Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan, the A-G, representing the Legislative Assembly Secretary, said, it was Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay who had moved the resolution on the floor of the House urging the Centre to not permit the State of Karnataka to construct the Mekedatu Dam across River Cauvery.

Then, the Leader of the Opposition, Udhayanidhi Stalin, had made a request to include an amendment urging the Centre to also constitute a new tribunal for resolving the dispute between the two States over the proposed construction of the dam. After thanking all members for having spoken in support of the resolution, the Chief Minister had agreed to carry out the amendment to the resolution.

Mr. Vijay had informed the House that a consultation meeting with legal experts was held under his leadership on the Mekedatu Dam issue on May 25, 2026 and that his government was already pursuing legal actions required for setting up a special tribunal for dealing exclusively with the Mekedatu Dam dispute. Therefore, he urged the Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar to include the amendment to the resolution.

After the Chief Minister’s speech, the Speaker had put to vote the amended resolution and declared it to have been passed unanimously by the House since no one, including the AIADMK whip Agri S.S. Krishnamurthy who had filed the present writ petition or his party general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami, had raised any objections to the amendment at that point of time, the A-G told the Division Bench.

On the other hand, senior counsel S.R. Rajagopal, representing the AIADMK whip, contested the submissions made by the A-G and claimed the amended resolution was never debated at all. The counsel said, the Assembly had debated and unanimously approved only the original resolution circulated to them a day before the Assembly session and not the amendment carried out at the last moment on June 19, 2026.

After hearing the preliminary submissions made by both sides, the judges ordered notices, returnable by August 14, to the Assembly Secretary, the Chief Secretary and the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti. The judges expected all the three respondents to file their counter affidavits to the writ petition, challenging the amended resolution, within two weeks.

World.title: Captain martyred, 7 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Hangu: ISPR
World.content:
The military media affairs wing said on Saturday that a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces conducted an IBO in Hangu on Friday following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, it said.

“In desperation, the khawarij took refuge inside a mosque, blatantly disregarding the sanctity of the place of worship. In ensuing fire exchange, seven khawarij, belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell,” it said.

The statement went on to say that during the exchange of fire, 27-year-old Captain Hamza Akram, a resident of Punjab’s Narowal district who was “leading his troops from front and relentlessly pursuing” the terrorists, embraced martyrdom.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed khawarij, who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies as well as killing of innocent civilians,” it said.

ISPR said that a sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists in the area.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the martyred captain saying, “The motherland pays its profound tribute to the great sacrifice of its brave son.”

“The entire nation is indebted to the eternal sacrifices of these brave sons for the motherland,” the president added, offering prayers for the bereaved family.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the martyred captain and offered his condolences to the bereaved family. He said that the martyred officer had paid the ultimate sacrifice for the homeland and would remain alive in our hearts.

A day earlier, ISPR said 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan, which was effectively thwarted, resulting in the deaths of eight terrorists.

“In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khawarij,” it added.

Terrorist commander killed in Bannu

Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander, identified as Jamidullah, during an operation in Jani Khel area of KP’s Bannu district, a security official said.

The official said that the terrorist commander was involved in terrorist activities and was considered a quadcopter expert.

The official said that security forces conducted the operation in Jani Khel on the basis of intelligence reports, during which Jamidullah was targeted and killed.

World.title: Efforts underway to end deadlock over judges’ appointments
World.content:
• Govt’s legal team set to meet Presidency officials as summary remains pending with Zardari

• Officials say matter now sub judice after petition filed in IHC

ISLAMABAD: In a last-ditch effort to break the deadlock over judicial appointments, the government’s legal team has scheduled a meeting with its counterparts at the Presidency on Sunday, as authorities explore the possibility of unilaterally notifying the confirmation and appointment of high court judges.

The development comes as the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has yet to issue its ruling on the maintainability of a petition challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s alleged failure to assent to the recommendations of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan.

The JCP, during its meetings on July 20 and 21, recommended the confirmation of four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court, a six-month extension for an additional judge of the Sindh High Court, and the appointment of 19 additional judges to the Lahore, Islamabad, Sindh and Balochistan high courts.

Under Clause 8 of Article 175-A of the Cons­titution, the recommendations were forwarded to the prime minister, who then sent the summary to the president. However, the summary has remained pending with the president since then.

Amid the stalemate, the government is examining the possibility of invoking Article 48(1) of the Constitution to issue the notifications through the law ministry, arguing that the president was required to act on the summary within a fortnight of its submission — a period that has since expired.

However, government functionaries have maintained that with the matter now sub judice, notifications cannot be issued at this stage.

Sources said the government’s legal team planned to pursue an “out-of-court” settlement with its counterparts at the Presidency.

The president’s legal team has raised certain objections to the JCP proceedings, noting that nearly all nominees proposed by the PPP were rejected. They also conveyed that some candidates recommended for appointment have criminal records.

The Presidency’s legal team contends that Article 175-A does not prescribe a specific timeframe for the president’s action and that the provision cannot be overridden by Article 48(1) to bypass the Presidency.

They have also referred to Article 48(2), which empowers the president “to act in his discretion in respect of any matter in respect of which he is empowered by the Constitution to do so” and states that validity of anything done by the president shall not be called into question on any ground whatsoever.

Sources in the Presidency cautioned that any unilateral action in such a sensitive matter would be a “political and legal disaster”. According to them, the only way forward is to reach a consensus through democratic means.

They warned that bypassing the prescribed procedure could trigger significant complications and suggested that any ambiguity regarding Articles 48(1), 48(2) and 175-A(8) should be resolved through mutual consultation between the president and the prime minister rather than through unilateral action.

On the other hand, government sources maintained that judicial appointments were governed by constitutional provisions and that any deadlock must be resolved strictly in accordance with the Constitution.

Meanwhile, the IHC has reserved its verdict on the maintainability of a petition filed by advocate Luqman Chaudhary through his counsel Zahid Chaudhry, seeking a direction to the president to approve the summary.

During Thursday’s hearing, Justice Arbab Muh­ammad Tahir questioned how the court could issue directions to the president and reserved his order.

It was initially expected that the ruling would be issued the same day, but Justice Arbab left his office without delivering it.

The order was then anticipated on Friday morning, but the file had not been returned from the judge’s chamber by the close of business.

The delay has already created practical complications. Four additional judges of the PHC, whose confirmations were recommended by the JCP, ceased to hold office after their tenure expired on Aug 4 due to the absence of formal notifications.

Similarly, an additional judge of the SHC, whose term was extended by six months, relinquished office after his tenure expired on July 29.

Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Malik said the government would resolve the matter within the constitutional framework and in accordance with the principles laid down by the superior courts.

Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan joins Saudi Arabia, Turkiye in ‘all for one’ pact
World.content:
• MBS, Shehbaz, Erdogan sign Makkah Joint Defence Agreement to boost ‘collective deterrence against any aggression’

• PM hopes accord will serve as ‘shield of peace’; Erdogan says alliance is open to other friendly nations • Saudi minister insists new bloc no threat to ‘any country’

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in the holy city of Makkah, which empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace.

The signing of the agreement was announced by three countries through a joint statement, which was published by Pakis­tan’s Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

It said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enha­ncement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

From Pakistan’s side, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well.

Following the formal signing of the pact, photos released by Saudi media showed the world leaders offering prayers at the Al-Safa Palace, overlooking the Holy Ka’aba.

‘Shield of peace’

PM Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”. “Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”. The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

‘Open to other nations’

Turkish President Erdogan also reiterated this sentiment, saying that the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace, prosperity and stability in the region.

In a post on the Turkish social platform NSosyal, Erdogan said on Friday the agreement, based on the principle of collective deterrence, would strengthen security and defence cooperation, joint defence industry projects and counterterrorism efforts. He said the agreement also reaffirms the right to self-defence as defined under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

“The agreement does not target any country and is open to the participation of all brotherly countries seeking peace, prosperity and stability in our region,” Erdogan said.

Türkiye, he added, would firmly maintain its principled stance in favour of resolving conflicts and crises through dialogue and diplomacy, based on respect for international law and in line with its vision of regional ownership.

Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.20, high-speed diesel by Rs1.50
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.20 and Rs1.50 per litre, respectively.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs327.62 per litre while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will apply from August 8 to 10.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: KP amends controversial law on lawmakers’ privileges
World.content:
• Provisions for lifetime blue passport scrapped; number of lifetime arms licences for MPAs reduced to four

• Assembly resolves to resist ‘proposed takeover’ of Hazara areas by federal government

PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Assembly on Friday withdrew controversial provisions from the recently enacted KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 2026, including the issuance of official passports to lawmakers and their spouses for life.

The provincial assembly had earlier in April passed the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Imm­unities and Privileges) Act, 2026, granting blue passports to members and their spouses, arms licences, blanket immunity from preventive detention, and making the speaker’s permission mandatory before arresting members on criminal charges.

However, the law faced harsh criticism from the media and the general public, prompting KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to order a review of the legislation last week. KP Information Minister Shafi Jan also announced that the government would withdraw the controversial clauses and restore the law in accordance with the 1988 Act.

According to the amendment tabled by treasury lawmaker Ghazi Ikram during a sitting chaired by KP Assembly Speaker Baber Saleem Swati, the house passed the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Amendment Act, 2026. The controversial provisions were withdrawn, and official passports will now remain valid only for the parliamentary tenure of lawmakers, in accordance with federal law. Also, the number of lifetime non-prohibited bore arms licences was also reduced from eight to four.

The concerns raised by the journalist community over enhanced fines and punishments were also addressed, with both fines and punishments being reduced.

Territorial integrity

The house also unanimously passed a resolution over the possible alteration of the territorial jurisdiction of KP by annexing some parts of the province to the federal territory. The resolution, moved by treasury lawmaker Akbar Ayub, stated that Haripur, Abbottabad and all other districts were integral parts of KP and could not be annexed to any other part of the country. It added that any changes — whether administrative, political, financial or aimed at controlling natural resources — would be against the law.

It stated that the residents of the province had constitutional rights over KP’s minerals, forests, hydel projects and other natural resources, and that any direct or indirect attempt to take control of these resources was unacceptable.

The resolution stated that any changes to the province’s geographical boundaries for personal interests or political objectives would violate the Constitution and could harm the federation. It strongly condemned any such plan and demanded that the federal government reject such suggestions and respect KP’s geographical, constitutional and administrative status.

The resolution added that the provincial assembly, the elected government and the people of KP would take all democratic and peaceful steps to safeguard the province’s geographical sovereignty, constitutional rights, provincial autonomy and natural resources, and would never hesitate to make any sacrifice.

The house appealed to all political parties, the legal fraternity, public representatives, civil society, youth and the media to make a joint effort to protect the province’s geographical boundaries and the constitutional rights of its residents. “This house warns the federal government to refrain from making any geographical changes, as such a step will never be acceptable to the people of KP and could harm inter-provincial harmony and national unity,” the resolution read, demanding that the federal government publicly reject any such proposal.

Source of revenue

During the sitting, MPA Fazal Ilahi said that annexing parts of KP was a conspiracy and was unacceptable, adding that the province generated significant revenue from those areas.

Earlier, treasury MPA Sultan-e-Rom informed the house that militancy had returned to Swat district after several years of relative peace. He questioned how long the people would continue to tolerate bombings.

He said militants began reappearing in 2022, but massive public protests against their presence helped restore relative normalcy. However, he added that explosions continued to occur across KP and recalled the bloodshed in Swat. “We would rather accept death than face displacement again,” he said.

Prescriptions

In her call-attention notice, opposition lawmaker Meher Sultana of the PPP informed the house that there was no law requiring doctors to prescribe medicines by their generic names rather than by brand names.

She said handwritten prescriptions were often illegible, placing an unnecessary financial burden on patients. She urged the health department to enact legislation requiring doctors to prescribe medicines by their generic names instead of brand names.

Health Minister Khal­eequr Rehman informed the house that the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the federal government because the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) registered medicines under brand names.

He said there was currently no policy requiring prescriptions by generic name but acknowledged that the issue was open to debate. However, he also argued that prescribing generic names could give medical store owners greater discretion to dispense medicines of their own choice.

Opposition lawmaker Shahida Waheed of the ANP informed the house that Mardan Medical Complex catered to patients from Mardan and several other districts, but its CT scan and MRI machines had remained out of order, causing immense hardship for patients.

Mr Zaman said the issue had been highlighted on social media and that notice had been taken. He said the CT scan machine was now functional and that the MRI machine would also be made operational soon.

The sitting was later adjourned until 2pm on Monday.

Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

World.title: Govt restores original medical board for exhumation of Mir Raza’s body
World.content:
• Corpse of IBA graduate to be dug up for fresh autopsy today

• Exhumation planned for Friday postponed after family objected to abrupt reconstitution of board
